invariants: Box is required and owns governed content.
Salesforce is required and owns structured business records.
The project must operate standalone and carry a Box Dispatch deployment interface.
Code, configuration, process diagram, storyboard, brief, tool/skill map, runbook, and acceptance checks are required.
No secrets in intake; tenant bindings remain in ignored runtime configuration.

questions.prompt: What should the project be called, and what lowercase kebab-case repository slug should it use?
What business problem and industry are we addressing, what is the current process, and what measurable outcome should improve?
Where does this workflow begin and end, and what is explicitly out of scope?
Should the first build be an offline demo or include implemented live Box and Salesforce adapters? Infrastructure deployment alone does not make the workflow live.

What languages/frameworks, hosting/runtime, licensing, existing-code, and deadline constraints apply? What user/document volumes, latency/reliability targets, and cost budget should the design support? Say none or request a concrete proposal where unrestricted.
Which coding agents and demo-facing AI clients should be supported, and what existing connectors, tools, models, or orchestration frameworks are available? Say none if starting fresh.
Should the project include an Agentforce agent written in Agent Script (an authoring bundle whose actions call the project's tools through Apex), or no Agentforce agent? Choose agent_script or none.
Who participates, what does each role do, and who owns the process?
Which employee or external-user surfaces are needed: headless agent, Salesforce workspace, portal, or other UI? What must each role see and do?

Should external users get a portal built as a Salesforce Multi-Framework React site (an Experience Cloud site running a React UI bundle, from the maintained site template), or no portal? Choose multi_framework_react_site or none.
What tenant, record, document, sensitive-data, and internal/external access boundaries must be enforced?
What starts the workflow? Describe the ordered steps, actor, input, action, expected output, and end state for each step.
Who owns each consequential decision, what evidence must they review, and which exact transitions/writes/generation/signature actions require their confirmation?
What can go wrong, when must the workflow stop or escalate, who receives exceptions, and how should it resume?

Which Salesforce objects and relationships are involved? Specify existing versus new objects, required fields and types, stable external IDs, and source-to-record mappings. If unknown, request a concrete proposal.
What record states and allowed transitions exist, and what rules or approvals permit each transition?
Which fields may the agent propose or update, which must remain human-owned, and how should current versions, permissions, duplicate records, and conflicting values be handled?

What document types/formats are required, what information is extracted or compared, and are approved sample documents available? Describe sample locations without supplying sensitive content or credentials.
What Box folder structure and metadata are needed? How does each Salesforce record map to its authorized Box folder, and how are files classified and versioned?
Which policies or approved knowledge sources govern decisions, what citations are required, and what retention, sharing, approval-status, or compliance rules apply? Say none where not applicable.
What exact validations, thresholds, calculations, units, authoritative values, and conflict-resolution rules must be implemented? Say none if there are no calculations.
Are generated documents needed? Identify document purpose, template/merge fields, output format and destination, required verification, and approval owner; otherwise say none.

Are signatures needed? Distinguish preparation from sending, signer roles, consent/approval gates, verified-file requirements, and completion evidence; otherwise say none. Do not provide signer credentials.
Who is the audience, what should they learn, how long is the demo, and what narrative, branding, or accessibility preferences matter?
Describe at least one successful case and one blocked/exception case. Include synthetic actors/documents, relevant sample values, expected evidence, and reset behavior.

The output always includes code/config, diagrams, storyboard, solution brief, tool/skill map, runbook, and acceptance checklist. What additional screenshots, decks, exports, UI views, or presentation formats are needed? Say none if the standard bundle is sufficient.
What observable results prove the use case works? Include happy path, blocked path, access refusal, stale data, exact output verification, and any domain-specific checks.

Both standalone operation and Box Dispatch deployment are required. Which infrastructure must be deployed, who operates it, and what idempotency, audit, rollback, cleanup, and environment-reset behavior is expected?

What integrations, entitlements, managed packages, org features, permission sets, reference links, source assets, or manual prerequisites are required? State unavailable or unknown items explicitly; do not assume they are installed.

Which non-secret Box tenant/parent-folder and Salesforce org aliases are intended, what environments are disposable, and who owns access? Store actual tenant IDs only in ignored runtime config; never paste tokens, client secrets, or passwords.

Which authenticated Box and Salesforce tools/endpoints and permissions are available for the required reads and writes? What evidence can verify their schemas, identities, and scope? Do not provide credentials.

What disposable data/resources and approved test scope can verify live success/failure, post-deployment record-to-folder binding, read-back, and cleanup? Intake confirmation itself does not authorize these external operations.
